title: Every writer of .bee/state.json holds the 'state' lock, on one global lock order
action: RED-FIRST, then fix, then vendor. (1) PROOF FIRST: create scripts/tests/test_state_projection_race.mjs modeled on scripts/tests/test_store_lock.mjs's shape — real OS child processes re-execing the same file with a --role flag (never in-process async: the writes are synchronous, an async 'race' never exercises them), a temp-repo fixture the test creates itself (nothing read from the live checkout, so no assertion can be satisfied by the ambient environment), a shared active.json mutual-exclusion detector writing violations.jsonl, and an exact final-count assertion over a counter driven through the same read-modify-write path. Role A = the state-sync shape: withStoreLock(root,'state', ... rebuildStateProjection). Role B = the CLI shape: withWorkflowLock(ctrlRoot, wf.id, ... rebuildStateProjection). Include a NEGATIVE CONTROL scenario running role B with the workflow lock ONLY (the pre-fix arrangement) which MUST produce violations — without it the suite can pass vacuously. Run this suite against unmodified bee.mjs and capture the RED output into the done-report before touching any source. (2) FIX packages/bee/bee.mjs at four seams: bee.mjs:2552 withMutationLock's `if (wf)` branch becomes withWorkflowLock(ctrlRoot, wf.id, () => withStoreLock(root, 'state', fn)) — the C1 'state' fallback branch at :2555 is deliberately NOT wrapped (lock.mjs is non-reentrant; double-wrapping self-deadlocks into LockBusyError); bee.mjs:3284 handleStateStartFeature's rebuildLaneProjection/rebuildStateProjection call wrapped in withStoreLock(root,'state', ...); bee.mjs:3304 handleStateRebuildProjections' rebuildAllProjections(root) wrapped in withStoreLock(root,'state', ...); and bee.mjs:2918-2950 handleStatePlanRevBump RESTRUCTURED from its current 'state'-outer/updateWorkflow-inner inversion to the canonical order — resolve the lane and workflow FIRST (outside both locks), then withWorkflowLock(ctrlRoot, wf.id, () => withStoreLock(root, 'state', body)) with updateWorkflowAssumingLock (NOT the self-locking updateWorkflow) inside. (3) Do NOT change rebuildStateProjection or rebuildLaneProjection in state-projection.mjs — they stay caller-serialized and acquire nothing, because bee-state-sync.mjs already holds 'state' when calling them. (4) VENDOR + REGEN, in this exact order, inside this cell: node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs, then node packages/bee/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply, then node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write. This repo executes the VENDORED copy, so md5sum of .bee/bin/bee.mjs must equal packages/bee/bee.mjs when done — report both sums in the done-report. An un-vendored fix ships nothing and the suite would still be exercising only the canonical source.

truths: scripts/tests/test_state_projection_race.mjs spawns real OS child processes and was proven RED against unmodified bee.mjs before any source edit, with that output captured in the done-report.
The suite carries a negative control (role B under the workflow lock only) that produces violations, proving the detector actually bites.
The suite's fixture is a temp repo the test creates; no assertion can be satisfied by the live checkout's ambient state.
The suite asserts the invariant 'every production writeState runs under the state lock', not a fixed enumeration of call sites.
withMutationLock's workflow branch nests 'state' inside workflow:<id>; the C1 'state' fallback branch is untouched.
bee.mjs:3284 and bee.mjs:3304 both write their projections under the 'state' lock.
handleStatePlanRevBump acquires workflow:<id> BEFORE 'state' and uses updateWorkflowAssumingLock inside, so workflow:<id> -> 'state' is the single global lock order in the repo.
md5sum of .bee/bin/bee.mjs equals packages/bee/bee.mjs after the change, both sums reported.
prohibitions: Do NOT acquire a lock inside rebuildStateProjection or rebuildLaneProjection — bee-state-sync.mjs already holds 'state' at that call and lock.mjs is non-reentrant, so it would throw LockBusyError on every hook tick.
Do NOT wrap withMutationLock's C1 'state' fallback branch — that is a same-name re-acquire from the same process.
Do NOT leave handleStatePlanRevBump on the old order; shipping the new edge without repairing that one is a deterministic ~5s dual LockBusyError, not a race.
Do NOT use setTimeout/Promise.all in one process to simulate concurrency; the race does not exist there.
Do NOT weaken, delete, or skip any existing test to make the suite green.
